source.title: Combining Explicit and Implicit Regularization for Efficient Learning in Deep Networks

page_placements.theme: Optimization induces conditional rank and spectral biases

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer and explicit-regularization effects on test error in matrix completion, a setting outside the claim versions’ specified natural-image and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports matrix-completion test error and effective rank under different depths, optimizers, and penalties. It does not test random-label memorization, natural-label classification, width scaling, dropout, large batches, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern linear matrix completion and rating prediction, not any specified claim version. Its optimizer comparisons do not test V4's image or language benchmarks and tuning conditions; its spectral ratio penalty tests neither dropout nor magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: optimizer, parameterization, loss, and architecture jointly shape generalization. In matrix completion, the ratio penalty combined with Adam enables accurate low-rank solutions even at depth 1. The authors do not conclude that explicit norm penalties fully characterize implicit regularization, and leave transfer to nonlinear networks and classification open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies deep linear networks and matrix completion with a proposed nuclear-norm/Frobenius-norm ratio penalty, rather than the natural-label classification and interventions specified by the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with optimizer, explicit penalty, and network depth. The ratio penalty's depth 1 effect is reported for Adam and not for gradient descent; Adam and Adamax perform best among the tested optimizer-penalty combinations. On MovieLens100K the reported result depends on train-test split and selected hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic rank 5 matrix completion, Adam with the ratio penalty reaches test error 4e-7 and effective rank 5 at depths 1 and 3. The penalty is ineffective with gradient descent at depth 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A spectral ratio penalty can interact with Adam to enable accurate low-rank matrix completion without depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Without a penalty, gradient descent has test error 0.83 and effective rank 72 at depth 1, versus 1e-5 and effective rank 5 at depth 3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth can improve gradient descent's rank recovery and reconstruction accuracy in linear matrix completion.

fits_no_version.finding: On MovieLens100K, adding the ratio penalty to depth 1 LNN Adam reduces RMSE from 1.844 to 0.915 on the 90:10 split and from 1.822 to 0.921 on the 80:20 split.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ratio penalty substantially improves this depth 1 linear rating predictor trained with Adam.

record.code_released: not stated; checklist says code is in supplementary material
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2022 (text states 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); supplied metadata lists Neural Information Processing Systems, 2023
record.problems: Experiments use linear networks on matrix completion, so their evidence does not establish behavior on the natural-label classification and language settings in the claim versions. Several principal comparisons are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The paper notes that its approximation of Adam dynamics is imperfect and that broader evaluation on nonlinear counterparts and other tasks remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows selected. Figures 1–4 and 6–8 report other depth, sample-size, rank, optimizer, and penalty comparisons, but the specified claim versions do not cover these matrix-completion conditions; figure values without explicit text descriptions are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Paired random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Width scaling beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization on image and language benchmarks under the specified tuning conditions, including the stated recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty; batch-size tuning alone does not test this.
Dropout effects, small-data failures, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row is outside their scope; this does not negate the reported matrix-completion effects. The synthetic test-error formula evaluates reconstruction against the full ground-truth matrix. No additional version-relevant result requires a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence; the paper studies matrix completion.
Width scaling past the interpolation threshold in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization on image-classification and language benchmarks under the version’s tuning conditions.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its removal alongside weight decay in classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap; effective rank is measured but is not the property named in this version.
Removing examples identified as memorized and measuring test accuracy.
